anchors.source_context_30_lines:
73: ### 4.1 Paper 15 Stabilization Discussion -- Now Closed
   74: 
   75: Paper 15 Section 3.10 identifies three routes to modulus stabilization: (a) $R_{g_K}^2$ corrections, (b) single-field potentials, (c) CW-type vacuum energy from boson masses (eq 3.87). Sessions 17-40 have systematically closed all of these:
   76: 
   77: | Paper 15 route | Closure gate | Session |
   78: |:---|:---|:---|
   79: | $R^2_{g_K}$ correction | Seeley-DeWitt $a_2/a_4$ | S20a |
   80: | Single-field slow-roll | $\eta \gg 1$ | S19b |
   81: | CW vacuum energy eq 3.87 | 1-loop CW insufficient | S18 |
   82: | Off-Jensen saddle | HESS-40, 22/22 positive | S40 |
   83: | Any spectral action cutoff | Structural monotonicity | S37 |
   84: 
   85: The spectral action route through Paper 15 is now exhausted by computation.
   86: 
   87: ### 4.2 Paper 17 Kosmann Derivative and QRPA
   88: 
   89: QRPA-40 finds $V_{\text{rem}}^{\text{odd}} = 0$ identically. The Kosmann-lifted pairing interaction is manifestly time-reversal invariant. This traces to Paper 17 eq 4.1: the Kosmann derivative $\mathcal{L}^K_X = \nabla_X + \frac{1}{4}\omega_{ab}\gamma^a\gamma^b$ involves the antisymmetric part of $\nabla_X e_a$, which is real and symmetric in its pairing-relevant matrix elements. The vanishing of $V_{\text{rem}}^{\text{odd}}$ is a representation-theoretic consequence of the Kosmann construction on $\operatorname{SU}(3)$, not a numerical accident.
